findings.description: AWS access key and secret key are hard-coded in plaintext as Lambda environment variables, exposing long-lived credentials to anyone with read access to the function configuration, console, or Terraform state, and risking leakage via logs or version control.

The Lambda function does not specify a KMS key (kms_key_arn) for environment variable encryption, so sensitive data (including the embedded credentials) is protected only by the default AWS-managed key rather than a customer-managed key, reducing control over key access and rotation.
The function uses nodejs12.x, an end-of-life Node.js runtime no longer receiving security patches from AWS, increasing exposure to unpatched vulnerabilities in the runtime itself.
